quoted.text: Interaction Rule: Most failures are induced by single factor faults or by the joint combinatorial effect (interaction) of two factors, with progressively fewer failures induced by interactions between three or more factors.
quoted.used_for: what a sweep that moves one control at a time structurally cannot see — the limit of this practice's own run of 2026-09-22

quoted.text: With the NASA application, for example, 67% of the failures were triggered by only a single parameter value, 93% by 2-way combinations, and 98% by 3-way combinations.
quoted.used_for: the order of magnitude of what one-way coverage does and does not reach, in the one field that has measured it

quoted.text: Collectively, therefore, this set of tests will exercise all 3-way combinations of input values in only 13 tests, as compared with 1,024 for exhaustive coverage.
quoted.used_for: the exchange this page is about, stated by a standards body twenty-six years before it: a product you cannot print against a sample you can

quoted.text: In general, the number of t-way combinatorial tests that will be required is proportional to v t log n, for n parameters with v possible values each.
quoted.used_for: why a covering array grows logarithmically in the number of controls where the product grows exponentially
quoted.note: the superscript on v is t; the PDF's text layer flattens it, and it is read here as v^t log n

quoted.text: A larger example system may have 10 devices to connect, in which case the number of permutations is 10!, or 3,628,800 tests for exhaustive testing. In that case, a 3-way sequence covering array with 14 tests covering all 10·9·8 = 720 3-way sequences is a dramatic improvement, as is 72 tests for all 4-way sequences.
quoted.used_for: the hands on this corpus that are made of buttons: a press leaves no state, so their space is one of sequences, and this is the construct that names it

quoted.text: We define a sequence covering array, SCA(N, S, t) as an N x S matrix where entries are from a finite set S of s symbols, such that every t-way permutation of symbols from S appears in at least one row.
quoted.used_for: the definition relied on for the sequence reading of a button hand
